@molecule/api-ai-classification.label: Ai Classification
@molecule/api-ai-classification.description: Zero-shot AI text classification core interface — score text against candidate labels with an LLM; default provider is @molecule/api-ai-classification-llm
@molecule/api-ai-classification.quickStart:
import { bond } from '@molecule/api-bond'
import { provider as anthropic } from '@molecule/api-ai-anthropic'
import { provider as classification } from '@molecule/api-ai-classification-llm'
import { requireProvider } from '@molecule/api-ai-classification'

// Wire an AI provider + the classifier at startup.
bond('ai', anthropic)
bond('ai-classification', classification)

// Use it anywhere.
const result = await requireProvider().classify({
  text: 'Win a FREE $1000 gift card now!!!',
  labels: ['spam', 'ham'],
})
console.log(result.top) // 'spam'
console.log(result.labels) // [{ label: 'spam', score: 0.98 }, { label: 'ham', score: 0.02 }]

secrets.name: FLY_API_TOKEN
secrets.label: Fly.io API token
secrets.instructions: Run `fly tokens create org <org>` (or `fly tokens deploy` for a single app). Needs permission to create apps, Machines and volumes in the org.

secrets.label: Sandbox OCI image
secrets.instructions: Image Fly pulls for each sandbox Machine. Must live in a registry Fly can reach — a local image is invisible to it.

secrets.label: Machines API base URL
secrets.instructions: Override the Machines API endpoint. From inside a Fly private network use http://_api.internal:4280.

secrets.name: FLY_SANDBOX_EGRESS_ALLOWED_PORTS
secrets.label: Sandbox egress allow-list (protocol:port)
secrets.instructions: Comma-separated protocol:port pairs a sandbox may open outbound connections on. Setting it makes the provider apply a Fly network policy to every sandbox app, after which Fly drops all other egress. Unset means NO egress restriction and verifyEgress() will report `open`. Fly matches protocol and port only — there is no host or CIDR matching — so allow only the port of an egress proxy you control if you need a host allow-list. Ports declared in FLY_SANDBOX_PRIVATE_SERVICES are added automatically — do not widen this list by hand.

secrets.name: FLY_SANDBOX_PRIVATE_SERVICES
secrets.label: Cross-6PN services (app:port)
secrets.instructions: Comma-separated <fly-app>:<port> pairs every sandbox must reach across its per-project 6PN — typically the tenant Postgres cluster and the control plane's egress proxy. The provider allocates a Flycast private address on each app INTO the project's own network at boot and releases it on destroy; the sandbox then dials <app>.flycast:<port>. Without this, a project with a database DOES NOT WORK on Fly: apps on separate 6PNs cannot communicate. Each target app needs an [http_service] or [services] section and must bind 0.0.0.0. The declared port is added to the egress network policy automatically.

fk-referential-action.note: DuckDB rejects ON DELETE and ON UPDATE CASCADE, SET NULL and SET DEFAULT at parse time and has no triggers, so a cascading or nulling delete cannot be reproduced. Select a database provider that enforces referential actions, or remove the resource whose schema needs them.

partial-index.note: Applied as a full index on the same columns. The WHERE clause only narrows which rows the index covers, so query results are identical without it.

unique-partial-index.note: Applied as a UNIQUE index over CASE WHEN <predicate> THEN <column> END for each indexed column. Rows outside the predicate get NULL keys, which DuckDB keeps distinct, so exactly the rows PostgreSQL would constrain are constrained.

secrets.name: MYSQL_URL

fk-referential-action.note: The translator hoists an inline REFERENCES into a table-level FOREIGN KEY and keeps ON DELETE/ON UPDATE, which InnoDB enforces (CASCADE, SET NULL, RESTRICT, NO ACTION). InnoDB does not implement SET DEFAULT.

partial-index.note: MySQL has no partial indexes; the bond applies a full index on the same columns. The WHERE clause only narrows which rows the index covers, so query results are unchanged.

unique-partial-index.note: MySQL has no partial indexes, and rebuilding this UNIQUE index from its column list would forbid rows PostgreSQL allows (for example a second non-default payment method). The bond refuses this construct before running the migration; select PostgreSQL, PGlite or SQLite, or remove the resource whose schema needs it.

@molecule/api-encryption-aes.description: AES-256-GCM encryption provider for molecule.dev — authenticated encryption, SHA-256 hashing, and key rotation

secrets.name: ENCRYPTION_KEY
secrets.label: AES-256 encryption key
secrets.instructions: 64-character hex (256-bit) key for AES-GCM encryption.

@molecule/api-encryption-aes.quickStart:
import { setProvider } from '@molecule/api-encryption'
import { provider } from '@molecule/api-encryption-aes'

// Wire the provider at startup (reads ENCRYPTION_KEY from env)
setProvider(provider)

// Or create with explicit config
import { createProvider } from '@molecule/api-encryption-aes'
const customProvider = createProvider({ key: 'your-64-char-hex-key' })
setProvider(customProvider)

// Stream a large file through chunked AES-256-GCM (1 MiB chunks by default)
import { createReadStream, createWriteStream } from 'node:fs'
import { pipeline } from 'node:stream/promises'
await pipeline(
  createReadStream('dump.sql'),
  customProvider.encryptStream({ context: 'backup:42', chunkBytes: 4 * 1024 * 1024 }),
  createWriteStream('dump.sql.enc'),
)
await pipeline(
  createReadStream('dump.sql.enc'),
  customProvider.decryptStream({ context: 'backup:42' }),
  createWriteStream('dump.sql'),
)

@molecule/api-leaderboard.label: Leaderboard Engine
@molecule/api-leaderboard.description: Generic ranked-aggregate engine: record metrics, compute leaderboards over daily/weekly/monthly/all-time windows with rank tie-breaking, scope isolation, and cron rollup.

setupSql.src/__setup__/leaderboard_events.sql:
-- Schema for @molecule/api-leaderboard.
--
-- Portable by design: this DDL is standard SQL that runs UNCHANGED on
-- PostgreSQL and SQLite, matching the service's dialect-agnostic contract
-- (the service touches the database only through @molecule/api-database's
-- abstract DataStore — no raw SQL). It deliberately uses NO dialect-only
-- functions:
--   * Row ids are generated by the DataStore's `create()` (which injects a
--     UUID when the caller omits one) — NOT a DB-side `gen_random_uuid()`,
--     which SQLite lacks. So the `id` columns carry no DB default.
--   * Timestamp defaults use the standard `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, not Postgres's
--     `now()` (also absent on SQLite).
-- The `UUID`/`TIMESTAMPTZ` type names and the partial index below are
-- PostgreSQL-native and accepted by SQLite via type affinity. MySQL's stricter
-- parser has them normalised automatically by the @molecule/api-database-mysql
-- bond at migrate time (UUID→CHAR(36), TIMESTAMPTZ→TIMESTAMP, partial-index
-- predicate dropped) — so no manual porting is required on any of the three
-- official database bonds.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "leaderboard_events" (
  "id" UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  "user_id" UUID NOT NULL,
  "metric" VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  "value" DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
  "scope_key" VARCHAR(128),
  "occurred_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  "createdAt" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_leaderboard_events_metric" ON "leaderboard_events" ("metric");
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_leaderboard_events_user" ON "leaderboard_events" ("user_id");
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_leaderboard_events_metric_occurred_at"
  ON "leaderboard_events" ("metric", "occurred_at");
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_leaderboard_events_scope"
  ON "leaderboard_events" ("metric", "scope_key", "occurred_at")
  WHERE "scope_key" IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "leaderboard_rollups" (
  "id" UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  "metric" VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  "window_kind" VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,
  "window_start" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  "window_end" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  "scope_key" VARCHAR(128),
  "user_id" UUID NOT NULL,
  "score" DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "rank" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "createdAt" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  "updatedAt" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  UNIQUE ("metric", "window_kind", "window_start", "scope_key", "user_id")
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_leaderboard_rollups_lookup"
  ON "leaderboard_rollups" ("metric", "window_kind", "window_start", "scope_key", "rank");

@molecule/api-leaderboard.quickStart:
import { recordMetric, getLeaderboard, rollupLeaderboard } from '@molecule/api-leaderboard'

await recordMetric('user-1', 'xp', 50)
await recordMetric('user-2', 'xp', 70)

const top = await getLeaderboard({
  metric: 'xp',
  window: 'weekly',
  limit: 10,
  tieBreak: 'earliest',
})

// Cron rollup (e.g. every hour)
await rollupLeaderboard({ metric: 'xp', window: 'weekly' })

@molecule/api-model-hosting.quickStart:
import { requireProvider, setProvider } from '@molecule/api-model-hosting'
import { provider as cloudRun } from '@molecule/api-model-hosting-cloud-run'
import { setProvider as setDecisions } from '@molecule/api-ai-decisions'
import { createProvider as createLaya } from '@molecule/api-ai-decisions-laya'

setProvider(cloudRun) // reads GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT + GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON on first use
const hosting = requireProvider()

const endpoint = await hosting.deploy({
  name: 'laya',
  image: 'us-docker.pkg.dev/acme/models/laya-serve:0.3.1',
  port: 8000,
  healthPath: '/health',
  accelerator: { kind: 'cpu' },
  cpu: 2,
  memoryMb: 4096,
  region: 'us',
  scaling: { minInstances: 0, maxInstances: 3, idleTimeoutSeconds: 900 },
  access: 'private',
})

setDecisions(createLaya({ baseUrl: endpoint.url, headers: () => hosting.authHeaders(endpoint.id) }))

@molecule/api-process-lifecycle.label: Process Lifecycle

@molecule/api-process-lifecycle-express.label: Express
@molecule/api-process-lifecycle-express.description: Express/Node process-lifecycle provider: GET /health/live and /health/ready, request tracking with Connection: close while draining, and SIGTERM/SIGINT graceful shutdown with ordered hooks.
@molecule/api-process-lifecycle-express.quickStart:
import { installExpressLifecycle } from '@molecule/api-process-lifecycle-express'
import { registerReadinessCheck, registerShutdownHook } from '@molecule/api-process-lifecycle'

const app = express()
const lifecycle = installExpressLifecycle({ app }) // mounts /health/live + /health/ready

registerReadinessCheck({ name: 'database', check: async () => db.ping() })
registerShutdownHook({ name: 'database-pool', run: () => db.pool.end() })

const server = app.listen(4000, () => lifecycle.markReady())
lifecycle.attachServer(server)

@molecule/api-project-archive-external-s.label: MotherDuck Databases

secrets.name: MOTHERDUCK_TOKEN
secrets.label: MotherDuck token
secrets.instructions: Needed only when a project owns MotherDuck databases. Create one in the MotherDuck UI: Settings → "+ Create token".
secrets.example: eyJhbGciOi... (the token the UI shows once at creation)

@molecule/api-project-archive-external-s.label: MySQL / MariaDB Database
@molecule/api-project-archive-external-s.description: MySQL external-state capture for project archives — mysqldump (routines, triggers, events) out, mysql client back in; refuses truncated dumps; env-only credentials.

secrets.name: PROJECT_ARCHIVE_MYSQL_URL
secrets.label: MySQL connection URL (archiver)
secrets.instructions: Connection string for the server holding project databases. The password is passed through a defaults file, never argv. Not needed if you inject your own connection config.

secrets.name: PROJECT_ARCHIVE_MYSQL_DATABASE
secrets.label: Project database name template
secrets.instructions: Database name for each project. MUST contain {projectId} — without it every project resolves to the same database, so one project's archive would hold another's data.

secrets.name: PROJECT_ARCHIVE_MYSQL_DUMP_BIN
secrets.label: mysqldump binary
secrets.instructions: Path to the mysqldump executable. Set it when the binary is not on PATH or is named differently (for example mariadb-dump).

secrets.name: PROJECT_ARCHIVE_MYSQL_CLIENT_BIN
secrets.label: mysql client binary
secrets.instructions: Path to the mysql client executable used to restore a dump. Set it when the binary is not on PATH or is named differently (for example mariadb).

secrets.name: PROJECT_ARCHIVE_MYSQL_MAX_DUMP_BYTES
secrets.label: Maximum dump size in bytes
secrets.instructions: Hard cap on a captured dump. A database that exceeds it fails the capture rather than being silently trimmed. Defaults to 256 MiB.

@molecule/api-project-archive-external-s.label: PGlite Data Directory
@molecule/api-project-archive-external-s.description: Back up and restore a project's PGlite database as part of a project archive — captures it with PGlite's own dumpDataDir, proves the dump loads back with the same row counts before the caller destroys anything, and restores it with loadDataDir after a checksum check. In-memory databases are declared, never inferred.

@molecule/api-project-archive-external-s.label: PostgreSQL Database
@molecule/api-project-archive-external-s.description: Back up and restore a project's PostgreSQL database as part of a project archive — captures it with pg_dump --format=custom into an archive part and puts it back with pg_restore, proving the dump decodes in full before the caller is allowed to destroy the original.

secrets.name: PROJECT_ARCHIVE_POSTGRESQL_URL
secrets.label: PostgreSQL connection URL (archiver)
secrets.instructions: Connection string for the server holding project databases. Credentials reach pg_dump/pg_restore through the environment, never argv. Not needed if you inject resolveDatabaseUrls instead.

secrets.name: PROJECT_ARCHIVE_POSTGRESQL_DATABASE
secrets.label: Project database name template
secrets.instructions: Database name for each project. MUST contain {projectId} — without it every project resolves to the same database, so one project's archive would hold another's data.

@molecule/api-project-archive-external-s.label: SQLite Database File
@molecule/api-project-archive-external-s.description: SQLite external-state capture for project archives — sqlite3 .dump SQL snapshot into the archive (consistent on a live database), replayed on restore.

secrets.name: PROJECT_ARCHIVE_SQLITE_PATH
secrets.label: Project database path template
secrets.instructions: Filesystem path of each project's SQLite database. MUST contain {projectId} — without it every project resolves to the same file. Not needed if you inject your own locate function.

secrets.name: PROJECT_ARCHIVE_SQLITE_ID
secrets.label: Database id recorded in the archive

-- Schema for @molecule/api-realtime-rooms.
--
-- Rooms are app-level pub/sub channels with persisted membership and
-- role-based authorisation. Membership rows fix the IDOR pattern in
-- flagship realtime apps: handlers MUST consult `realtime_room_members`
-- (via assertCanAct()) before broadcasting / subscribing.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "realtime_rooms" (
  "id" UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  "kind" VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  "owner_id" UUID NOT NULL,
  "capacity" INTEGER,
  "join_code" VARCHAR(64),
  "is_public" BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  "created_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_realtime_rooms_kind" ON "realtime_rooms" ("kind");
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_realtime_rooms_owner" ON "realtime_rooms" ("owner_id");

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "realtime_room_members" (
  "room_id" UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES "realtime_rooms" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
  "user_id" UUID NOT NULL,
  "role" VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL CHECK ("role" IN ('host', 'guest')),
  "joined_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY ("room_id", "user_id")
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_realtime_room_members_room"
  ON "realtime_room_members" ("room_id");
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_realtime_room_members_user"
  ON "realtime_room_members" ("user_id");

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "articles" (
  "id" UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  "slug" VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  "title" VARCHAR(300) NOT NULL,

  "updatedAt" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "article_tags" (
  "id" UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  "articleId" UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES "articles"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
  "tag" VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  -- The order the tag was given in (0-based). Without it a reader of this table
  -- gets the tags in whatever order the database returns rows, which is not the
  -- order the article was submitted with.
  "position" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "createdAt" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE ("articleId", "tag")
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "idx_article_tags_tag" ON "article_tags" ("tag");
setupSql.src/__setup__/articles_position.sql:
-- Tag order on an article: the column "article_tags"."position" keeps the order
-- the tags were given in, so a reader of the join table (a tag filter, an app's
-- own query) gets them in that order instead of the database's arbitrary row
-- order.
--
-- Why this is its own file: a database that already applied articles.sql never
-- re-runs it — "_molecule_migrations" records each setup file once — so the
-- column cannot be delivered by editing that file alone. This file is new, so it
-- runs on every database that has the table, whether it was created before or
-- after the column existed.
--
-- The CREATE repeats articles.sql's "article_tags" (see the test that keeps the
-- two in step). In a scaffolded app it is a no-op — articles.sql sorts first and
-- has already created the table, so the column below is what this file is for —
-- and it is what lets the scaffolding tool find the file at all: a setup file is
-- copied into a project through the table it declares.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "article_tags" (
  "id" UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  "articleId" UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES "articles"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
  "tag" VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  "position" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  "createdAt" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  UNIQUE ("articleId", "tag")
);

-- The upgrade for a database whose "article_tags" predates the column. Every
-- database bond accepts this form: Postgres and PGlite take the clause natively,
-- and the SQLite and MySQL bonds apply the statement only when the column is not
-- there yet.
ALTER TABLE "article_tags" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "position" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

configuration: For a custom HTTP handler, import { follow, unfollow, isFollowing, getFollowedIds } from '@molecule/api-resource-follow'. Resolve the route parameter to a canonical target id and call follow(viewerId, targetType, id), unfollow(viewerId, targetType, id) or isFollowing(viewerId, targetType, id). Keep your paths, validation and response mapping in the handler.

The services share the installed follows(followerId, targetType, targetId) table. A custom handler can use it without mounting the package routes. For a public view, use viewerId ? await isFollowing(viewerId, targetType, id) : false. Different relationship schemas stay local.

For a displayed collection, call getFollowedIds(viewerId, targetType, ids) once and join with followed.has(id). It returns a Set of followed canonical ids, deduplicates the input, and does no database reads for an absent viewer or empty collection. Target types can be users, documents, topics or any application resource.
getFollowing(viewerId, options) pages across target types. To enumerate every followed id for one type, page and filter its results or query the same follows table by followerId and targetType.

-- Table for the notification-center database provider
-- (@molecule/api-notification-center-database). Column names are snake_case to
-- match that provider's contract: it create()s { user_id, type, title, body,
-- read, data, channels, created_at } and findMany()s WHERE user_id / read / type
-- ORDER BY created_at, and maps rows back via row.user_id / row.created_at. A
-- previous stub shipped only id + camelCase "createdAt"/"updatedAt", so
-- GET /api/notifications 500'd at runtime ("column ... does not exist") on every
-- out-of-the-box build. `channels` is REQUIRED too: the provider's send()
-- always writes it (JSON-serialized delivery channels, null default) — without
-- the column every create() fails with "column channels does not exist".
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "notifications" (
  "id" UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  "user_id" UUID NOT NULL,
  "type" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "title" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "body" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "read" BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  "data" JSONB,
  "channels" JSONB,
  "created_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  "updated_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "notifications_user_id_idx" ON "notifications" ("user_id");
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "notifications_user_id_read_idx" ON "notifications" ("user_id", "read");

-- Preferences table for the same provider (its getPreferences/setPreferences):
-- one row per user with per-channel booleans + a JSON `channels` map of
-- per-type overrides. Nothing else in the fleet creates this table, so without
-- it GET /api/notifications/preferences 500s out of the box.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "notification_preferences" (
  "id" UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  "user_id" UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  "email" BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  "push" BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  "sms" BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  "channels" JSONB,
  "created_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  "updated_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

setupSql.src/__setup__/orders_position.sql:
-- Line-item order on an order: the column "order_items"."position" keeps the
-- order the items were submitted in, so a reader of this table (the read/list/
-- cancel/updateStatus handlers, an app's own query) gets them in that order
-- instead of the database's arbitrary row order. `where "orderId" = ?` hits
-- "idx_order_items_orderId", so without this column the rows come back in the
-- index's order — not the order the customer submitted.
--
-- Why this is its own file: a database that already applied orders.sql never
-- re-runs it — "_molecule_migrations" records each setup file once — so the
-- column cannot be delivered by editing that file alone. This file is new, so it
-- runs on every database that has the table, whether it was created before or
-- after the column existed.
--
-- The CREATE repeats orders.sql's "order_items" (see the test that keeps the two
-- in step). In a scaffolded app it is a no-op — orders.sql sorts first and has
-- already created the table, so the column below is what this file is for — and
-- it is what lets the scaffolding tool find the file at all: a setup file is
-- copied into a project through the table it declares.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "order_items" (
  "id" UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  "orderId" UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES "orders" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
  "productId" VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  "variantId" VARCHAR(255),
  "name" VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  "price" NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL,
  "quantity" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  "image" TEXT,
  "position" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

-- The upgrade for a database whose "order_items" predates the column. Every
-- database bond accepts this form: Postgres and PGlite take the clause natively,
-- and the SQLite and MySQL bonds apply the statement only when the column is not
-- there yet.
ALTER TABLE "order_items" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "position" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

@molecule/api-slug.label: Slugs
@molecule/api-slug.description: URL slugs from titles and names: accent-folding slugify, and unique slugs checked against your store (a table column or any lookup).

configuration: For a bonded database table, import { uniqueSlugInTable } from '@molecule/api-slug' and call uniqueSlugInTable(table, column, title, { excludeId, fallback }). Pass the current row id as excludeId on update. The helper normalizes the title and tries the plain slug, then numbered suffixes. Keep the unique index to protect concurrent inserts.

For a custom lookup, import { uniqueSlug } from '@molecule/api-slug' and call uniqueSlug(title, isTaken, options). isTaken(slug) returns true for an occupied candidate, synchronously or via a promise. Use slugify(title, options) from the same package when only normalization is needed.

@molecule/app-auth.label: Authentication

header: The first session read starts restoration even when the app entry omits `initialize()`. A stored token and cached user restore synchronously. Token-only and cookie-only restores are asynchronous. A visitor without a session candidate is signed out immediately. `getAccessToken()` returns the stored token during restore. With `storage: 'memory'` a session restored from the httpOnly cookie has no token, so decide signed-in from the session status or user.

`validateSession()` rechecks the session. HTTP 401/403 clears it by default. Set `currentUserRejectionStatuses` for extra 4xx codes from the current-user route that explicitly reject the session. Network/5xx failures keep it as `unavailable`.

`tokenKey`/`storagePrefix`, `authScheme`, `mapAuthResponse`, `currentUserEndpoint`, and `profileEndpoint`/`profileUpdateMethod` adapt the API; `logout()` and `refresh()` are included. A token another tool reads at its own storage key (an e2e suite, a legacy script) uses `tokenKey` and the default browser storage.

Save the signed-in profile with authClient.updateProfile(changes): it stores and publishes the server response. An app-owned HTTP mutation must call authClient.setUser(savedUser) with its canonical response before navigation; getUser() otherwise keeps the cached profile.

Read the session through the declared framework binding below. The session status is `loading` | `authenticated` | `unauthenticated` | `unavailable`. A session boundary holds its children only while the status is `loading`. The HTTP gate waits for restore before sending requests.
This file is the app's ONE session store — never add another token or user store beside it.
Sharing `tokenKey` does not make a second context/provider an adapter: copied user/status, token helpers or a restore effect are a second session store; view/debug adapters read the bonded client.

declarations.createJWTAuthClient: function createJWTAuthClient<T extends AuthProfileConstraint<T> = UserProfile, TRegister extends RegisterExtraShape<TRegister> = Record<never, never>>(config?: NoInfer<AuthClientConfigOptions<T>>): AuthClient<T, TRegister>;

@molecule/app-react: Read the session with `useAuth()` from `@molecule/app-react`. `state.status` is the session status and `state.user` is the current user. `AuthProvider` holds children only while the session is loading by default.

For editable account forms, use `useProfileForm` to hydrate pristine fields without erasing edits. An existing form can save with `useAuth<MyUser>().updateProfile(changes)`; a custom mutation calls `setUser(savedUser)` before navigation. A one-time useState seed does not follow a late user.
@molecule/app-vue: Read the session with `useAuth()` from `@molecule/app-vue`: `state.value.status` is the session status and `user.value` is the current user. The scaffold provides the client with `app.use(moleculePlugin, { auth: authClient, … })` in src/main.ts.

For editable account forms, use `useProfileForm` from `@molecule/app-vue` to hydrate pristine fields without erasing edits. An existing form can save with `useAuth<MyUser>().updateProfile(changes)`; a custom mutation calls `setUser(savedUser)` before navigation. A one-time `ref` seed does not follow a late user.
@molecule/app-svelte: Read the session with `const { state, user } = useAuth()` from `@molecule/app-svelte`: `$state.status` is the session status and `$user` is the current user. The scaffold provides the client with `setMoleculeContext({ auth: authClient, … })` in src/routes/+layout.svelte.

For editable account forms, use `useProfileForm` from `@molecule/app-svelte` to hydrate pristine fields without erasing edits. An existing form can save with `useAuth<MyUser>().updateProfile(changes)`; a custom mutation calls `setUser(savedUser)` before navigation. A one-time `$state` seed does not follow a late user.
@molecule/app-solid: Read the session with `useAuth()` from `@molecule/app-solid`. `state().status` is the session status and `user()` is the current user. The scaffold provides the client with `<MoleculeProvider config={{ auth: authClient, awaitSession: true }}>` in src/App.tsx.

For editable account forms, use `useProfileForm` from `@molecule/app-solid` to hydrate pristine fields without erasing edits. An existing form can save with `useAuth<MyUser>().updateProfile(changes)`; a custom mutation calls `setUser(savedUser)` before navigation. A one-time `createSignal` seed does not follow a late user.
@molecule/app-angular: Read the session with `readonly auth = useAuth()` from `@molecule/app-angular`, as a component field: `auth.state().status` is the session status and `auth.user()` is the current user. The scaffold provides the client with `provideMolecule({ auth: authClient, … })` in src/main.ts.

For editable account forms, use `useProfileForm` from `@molecule/app-angular` to hydrate pristine fields without erasing edits. An existing form can save with `useAuth<MyUser>().updateProfile(changes)`; a custom mutation calls `setUser(savedUser)` before navigation. A one-time field seed does not follow a late user.
@molecule/app-react-native: Read the session with `useAuth()` from `@molecule/app-react-native`. `state.status` is the session status and `state.user` is the current user. `AuthProvider` holds children only while the session is loading by default.

configuration: Request and response shapes are independent. Flat login/register bodies need no mapper. When the API reads a named envelope, configure mapRequestBody: (payload: Record<string, unknown>) => ({ account: payload }) with its actual envelope key; mapAuthResponse only reads the answer. Profile writes use their own profileRequestBody: (payload: unknown) => ({ account: payload }). Keep the generated auth bond and the framework auth binding; do not wrap credentials at a page call or add another session store.

Bearer + top-level token: keep `authScheme: 'Bearer'` and the default response mapping; set `currentUserEndpoint` and `profileEndpoint`/`profileUpdateMethod` to the API's current-user GET and profile update route/method.

Custom token API: set `tokenKey` (or `storagePrefix`), `authScheme: 'Token'`, `currentUserEndpoint`, and `profileEndpoint`/`profileUpdateMethod`; use `mapAuthResponse` to turn envelopes such as `{ user: { token, ...user } }` into `{ accessToken, user }`.

Cookie session: use `storage: 'memory'`, `cookieRestore: 'always'`, configure `currentUserEndpoint`, and keep HTTP `withCredentials: true`; no browser token store is needed. The default `cookieRestore: 'hint'` probes only when the server also sets a readable `mol_auth=1` presence cookie.

When login, registration and profile writes share a body wrapper, configure requestEnvelope: 'member' once to send { member: values } for all three. Explicit mapRequestBody and profileRequestBody override individual operations; mapRequestBody alone applies only to login/register.

@molecule/app-client-search.quickStart:
import { createIndex, setProvider } from '@molecule/app-client-search'
import { provider } from '@molecule/app-client-search-minisearch'

setProvider(provider)

const index = createIndex(packages, {
  idField: 'name',
  fields: ['name', 'description', 'exports'],
  filterFields: ['category', 'type', 'stack'],
  boost: { name: 3 },
})

index.search('category:auth oauth') // auth packages mentioning OAuth, best first
index.search('"sign in" -deprecated') // the phrase, minus anything deprecated
index.search({ text: '', filters: [{ field: 'type', values: ['bond'] }] }) // browse mode

@molecule/app-e2e-playwright.label: E2E via Playwright
@molecule/app-e2e-playwright.description: Real Playwright browsers for the e2e bond — the user's machine and CI
@molecule/app-e2e-playwright.quickStart:
// e2e/bonds.ts (scaffolded)
import { resolveE2EProviderName, setProvider } from '@molecule/app-e2e'
import { provider as playwright } from '@molecule/app-e2e-playwright'
import { provider as preview } from '@molecule/app-e2e-preview'

setProvider(resolveE2EProviderName() === 'preview' ? preview : playwright)

// a script
import { connectPlaywright } from '@molecule/app-e2e-playwright'
const page = await connectPlaywright({
  baseURL: 'http://localhost:3000',
  viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 },
})
await page.goto('/')
await page.screenshot({ path: 'home-phone.png' })
await page.close() // closes the context and the browser too

@molecule/app-e2e-preview.label: E2E via Live Preview
@molecule/app-e2e-preview.description: Drives the live IDE preview page as a Playwright-shaped page over a same-origin WebSocket through the dev server — no browser binary in the sandbox
@molecule/app-e2e-preview.quickStart:
// e2e/bonds.ts (scaffolded)
import { resolveE2EProviderName, setProvider } from '@molecule/app-e2e'
import { provider as playwright } from '@molecule/app-e2e-playwright'
import { provider as preview } from '@molecule/app-e2e-preview'

setProvider(resolveE2EProviderName() === 'preview' ? preview : playwright)

// vite.config.ts (scaffolded) — every molecule preview plugin in one entry
import { stripPreviewBridgePlugin } from '@molecule/app-e2e-preview/vite'
config.plugins = [...(config.plugins ?? []), stripPreviewBridgePlugin()]

// any script — measure the live page without a test runner
import { connectPreview } from '@molecule/app-e2e-preview'
const page = await connectPreview()
await page.setViewportSize({ width: 390, height: 844 })
console.log(
  await page
    .locator('article p')
    .first()
    .evaluate((el) => getComputedStyle(el).fontSize),
)
await page.close()

@molecule/app-http.label: HTTP Client
@molecule/app-http.description: HTTP client with interceptors and providers

header: This is the app's ONE HTTP client — every page call goes through it.

It reads the auth client's token through `setAuthTokenSource(() => authClient.getAccessToken())`, so this client AND one bonded later send the current session token with their configured `authScheme`; it also holds requests until session restore settles (`setAuthGate(() => authClient.whenRestored())`).

Keep BOTH halves when replacing this file: waiting for restore does NOT attach a token. Prefer the shared source over a one-client interceptor, and pass `authConfig.authScheme` to the transport constructor.

@molecule/app-bonds-default-react: React default binding: when replacing the composition, use `createDefaultHttpClientWithAuthBearer({ baseURL, getToken: () => authClient.getAccessToken(), authScheme })` from `@molecule/app-bonds-default-react` instead of a bare `createFetchClient`.

configuration: Bearer or another token scheme: construct the bonded client with `baseURL` and `authScheme: 'Bearer'` (or `authScheme: 'Token'`); pass the shared `authConfig.authScheme` rather than attaching headers per request.
Cookie sessions: construct with `withCredentials: true`; the browser sends the cookie, so no Authorization interceptor or token store is needed.
Session restore: keep `setAuthTokenSource` for the current token and `setAuthGate` for restore; delaying a request alone does not attach its credential.

Custom HTTP session restore: use setAuthGate({ client, restore }) with the bonded client. The callback's request uses its token and interceptors and bypasses the gate even after an await. Ordinary requests still wait for the restore.

@molecule/app-query.label: Query Cache
@molecule/app-query.description: Client-side data cache and prefetch core interface for molecule.dev — fetch once, read synchronously, warm ahead of navigation; the cache engine is a bond

configuration: POST/DELETE relationships: use createQueryResource({ name, path, id, http: getClient, readOne }).toggle(viewer, id, action, desired). true sends POST and false sends DELETE; desired is the state wanted after the request. readOne selects the saved record from this API's response envelope.

Return the saved flag from the commit of useOptimisticToggle or OptimisticToggleButton; for a flag with a count, return both from useOptimisticValue. Verify persistence by reloading and reading the dependent list. APIs that instead accept a boolean PUT/PATCH body use update() or their own explicit adapter.

intentHints: record action path with required id
@molecule/app-query.quickStart:
import { getClient } from '@molecule/app-http'
import { getQueryClient, setProvider } from '@molecule/app-query'
import { provider } from '@molecule/app-query-tanstack'

setProvider(provider)

const packageQuery = (name: string) => ({
  key: ['package', name],
  fetch: async (signal: AbortSignal) =>
    (await getClient().get(`/data/packages/${encodeURIComponent(name)}.json`, { signal })).data,
})

const client = getQueryClient()
client.prefetch(packageQuery('api-auth')) // on hover: warm it
const doc = client.get(['package', 'api-auth']) // later, synchronously
await client.fetch(packageQuery('api-auth')) // or wait for it
client.invalidate(['package']) // every package is stale now

@molecule/app-query-angular.label: Query Cache Angular
@molecule/app-query-angular.description: Angular hooks for @molecule/app-query — read a cached document synchronously, observe it, and prefetch on intent

configuration: API lists and detail reads: import { useQuery } from "@molecule/app-query-angular"; in a component field initializer, readonly query = useQuery(computed(() => ({ key: [http.baseURL, path, viewer, params], fetch: async (signal) => (await http.get(path, { signal, params })).data }))); render query.data directly in the template; outside the item list, render a role="status" line while its status is 'idle' or 'loading', a role="alert" line when it is 'error', and the empty state when the list is empty. Use the already bonded query provider in src/bonds/. The computed re-reads its inputs, so a changed key follows on the same component.

One visible collection has one query whose key includes every request input (record, filter/view, page and the viewer when personalized). Pass null until required inputs or session restore are ready. A late response for another key cannot overwrite this key. For same-viewer page changes, keepPreviousData requires principal: viewer. Local arrays and non-data effects stay local.

@molecule/app-routing.label: Routing
@molecule/app-routing.description: Client-side routing with guards and navigation

configuration: URL-backed lists (`?page=2`, `?status=open`, a tab such as Mine/All, `/category/:slug`): keep the page, filters and tab in the URL only, read and change them through the declared framework binding, and return to page one when a filter or tab changes.
Signed-in-only views reached by URL: wait for the session restore, then send only a confirmed signed-out visitor to the sign-in page with a return path; an unavailable session is not signed out.

@molecule/app-routing-angular-router.label: Angular Router

configuration: Angular Router URL lists: `readonly list = useListRoute({ pageSize: 20 })` from `@molecule/app-angular`, as a component field. Each field is a signal: use `list.page()`, `list.offset()` and `list.params()` for requests and `list.href({ page: 2 })` for links; filter or selection changes reset to page one. Pass a signal (`computed(() => ({ … }))`) when the options read reactive state. Do not mirror URL values in signals.

The URL alone selects the view: hiding its link does not guard a direct visit. Protected views use `requiresAuth: true` and `auth: { status, redirectTo }`; load only while `canLoad` is true. Only a confirmed `unauthenticated` status redirects (with `state.returnTo`); `loading` and `unavailable` wait. Example: `useListRoute(computed(() => ({ selections: { all: { path: '/orders' }, mine: { path: '/orders', query: { view: 'mine' }, requiresAuth: true } }, auth: { status: this.auth.status(), redirectTo: '/login' } })))`, with `readonly auth = useAuth()` from `@molecule/app-angular`.

A one-time credential (reset token or OAuth `code`): `readonly token = useConsumedSearchParam('token')` from `@molecule/app-angular` keeps the value and removes that URL key; read `token[0]` in the template, clear it with `token[1]('')`. `src/main.ts` provides `provideMoleculeRouter()` next to `provideRouter(routes)`; keep both.

@molecule/app-routing-react-router.label: React Router
@molecule/app-routing-react-router.description: React Router provider with URL-backed list pagination, filters, path/query selections and auth readiness

configuration: Declare a parameterized page with defineRoute(path, { Component: Page }). Page receives a typed params prop directly from React Router. Use the callback form when the route also supplies local props. Retain the returned declaration and call route.href(params) from links and post-save callbacks. Use the saved response for the route parameter when the save can change it.

URL-selected tabs or list views: render `ListRouteNav` from this package. Pass `selections={{ all: { path: "/orders", query: { view: undefined }, label: t("orders.all", undefined, { defaultValue: "All orders" }) }, open: { path: "/orders", query: { view: "open" }, label: t("orders.open", undefined, { defaultValue: "Open orders" }) } }}` and a translated `aria-label`. The shared declaration keeps every choice visible across related routes; links navigate to their declared path and reset page through useListRoute. Active styling comes from the URL. Use `Tabs` from the UI package for genuinely local panels. Render the results as the children function and use its selection, params and page for the data request. That keeps the result and active link bound to the same URL, with the filters visible while results load.

React Router URL lists: start with `const pages = useListRoute()` from `@molecule/app-routing-react-router`; `filters` and `selections` are optional. Use `page`, `offset` and `params` for requests, `href({ page: 2 })` for links. Pass `pageSize` (default 20) to match the request limit and footer; `offset` is `(page - 1) * pageSize`. Do not mirror URL values in state.

A route with its own path params uses the hook unchanged: on `/category/books` matched by `/category/:slug`, `pages.href({ page: 2 })` is `/category/books?page=2`, without a duplicate query filter. On `/?view=mine` it is `/?view=mine&page=2` (existing query order, page last). Page one omits `page`; unrelated queries and hash survive. Filter or selection changes reset page atomically. Add `path` only to change path params, or `selections` to link between views.

The URL alone selects the view: hiding its link or combining a URL match with user availability does not guard a direct visit. Protected views use `requiresAuth: true` and `auth: { status, redirectTo }`; load only with `canLoad`. Adapt an app-owned session: `const routeAuthStatus = restoring ? 'loading' : failed ? 'unavailable' : user ? 'authenticated' : 'unauthenticated'`. Keep `restoring` true until restoration decides. Only confirmed `unauthenticated` redirects, with `state.returnTo`; `loading` and `unavailable` wait. Example: `const list = useListRoute({ selections: { all: { path: '/orders' }, mine: { path: '/orders', query: { view: 'mine' }, requiresAuth: true } }, auth: { status: routeAuthStatus, redirectTo: '/login' } })`. `list.href({ selection: 'all' })` resets to `/orders` from `/orders?view=mine&page=4`.

Other query reads can use `useMoleculeQuery()` inside your existing React Router. A one-time credential (reset token or OAuth `code`) uses `useConsumedSearchParam(name)`: `const [token] = useConsumedSearchParam('token')` retains the value and removes that URL key. Neither hook needs `MoleculeRouterProvider`. Native query defaults/options and other uncovered operations can stay local.

@molecule/app-routing-solid-router.label: Solid Router

configuration: Solid Router URL lists: `const list = useListRoute(() => ({ pageSize: 20 }))` from `@molecule/app-solid`. Each field is an accessor: use `list.page()`, `list.offset()` and `list.params()` for requests and `list.href({ page: 2 })` for links; filter or selection changes reset to page one. Pass the options as a function so reactive values re-resolve. Do not mirror URL values in signals.

The URL alone selects the view: hiding its link does not guard a direct visit. Protected views use `requiresAuth: true` and `auth: { status, redirectTo }`; load only while `canLoad` is true. Only a confirmed `unauthenticated` status redirects (with `state.returnTo`); `loading` and `unavailable` wait. Example: `useListRoute(() => ({ selections: { all: { path: '/orders' }, mine: { path: '/orders', query: { view: 'mine' }, requiresAuth: true } }, auth: { status: auth.status(), redirectTo: '/login' } }))`, with `const auth = useAuth()` from `@molecule/app-solid`.

A one-time credential (reset token or OAuth `code`): `const token = useConsumedSearchParam('token')` from `@molecule/app-solid` keeps the value and removes that URL key; read `token[0]` where it is used (a destructured copy is not reactive), clear it with `token[1]('')`. `src/App.tsx` builds the router with `createSolidRouter()` inside `<Router root>`; keep the providers there.

@molecule/app-routing-solid-router.quickStart:
import { MemoryRouter, Route } from '@solidjs/router'
import { MoleculeProvider } from '@molecule/app-solid'
import { createSolidRouter } from '@molecule/app-routing-solid-router'

;<MemoryRouter
  history={memory}
  root={(props) => (
    <MoleculeProvider router={createSolidRouter({ history: memory })}>
      {props.children}
    </MoleculeProvider>
  )}
>
  <Route path="/users/:id" component={User} />
  <Route path="*rest" component={NotFound} />
</MemoryRouter>

@molecule/app-routing-sveltekit.label: SvelteKit

configuration: SvelteKit URL lists: `const { page, offset, params, href } = useListRoute({ pageSize: 20 })` from `@molecule/app-svelte`. Each field is a store: use `$page`, `$offset` and `$params` for requests and `href({ page: 2 })` for links; filter or selection changes reset to page one. Pass a store of options when they depend on reactive state. Read the location through the molecule router, not `$page` from `$app/stores`.

The URL alone selects the view: hiding its link does not guard a direct visit. Protected views use `requiresAuth: true` and `auth: { status, redirectTo }`; load only while `canLoad` is true. Only a confirmed `unauthenticated` status redirects (with `state.returnTo`); `loading` and `unavailable` wait. Example: `useListRoute(derived(state, ($state) => ({ selections: { all: { path: '/orders' }, mine: { path: '/orders', query: { view: 'mine' }, requiresAuth: true } }, auth: { status: $state.status, redirectTo: '/login' } })))`, with `const { state } = createAuthStores()` from `@molecule/app-svelte` and `derived` from `svelte/store`.

A one-time credential (reset token or OAuth `code`): `const token = useConsumedSearchParam('token')` from `@molecule/app-svelte` keeps the value and removes that URL key; read `$token[0]`, clear it with `$token[1]('')`. `src/routes/+layout.svelte` builds the router with `createSvelteKitRouter(createSvelteKitNavigation({ goto, page, afterNavigate, rootHref: resolve('/') }))`; keep it in the root layout.

@molecule/app-routing-sveltekit.quickStart:
<!-- src/routes/+layout.svelte -->
<script lang="ts">
  import { goto } from '$app/navigation'
  import { resolve } from '$app/paths'
  import { navigating, page } from '$app/state'
  import {
    createSvelteKitNavigation,
    MoleculeRouterProvider,
  } from '@molecule/app-routing-sveltekit'

  // Build the navigation here, in the root layout's initialisation, once: it watches kit's
  // `page` from there. `resolve('/')` gives the bond the base path (or `#` under hash
  // routing) kit's `goto` and links need.
  const navigation = createSvelteKitNavigation({ goto, page, navigating, rootHref: resolve('/') })
</script>

<MoleculeRouterProvider {navigation}>
  {@render children()}
</MoleculeRouterProvider>

@molecule/app-routing-vue-router.label: Vue Router

configuration: Vue Router URL lists: `const list = useListRoute({ pageSize: 20 })` from `@molecule/app-vue` returns a computed ref. Use `list.value.page`, `list.value.offset` and `list.value.params` for requests and `list.value.href({ page: 2 })` for links; filter or selection changes reset to page one. Pass a getter (`() => ({ … })`) when the options read reactive state. Do not mirror URL values in refs.

The URL alone selects the view: hiding its link does not guard a direct visit. Protected views use `requiresAuth: true` and `auth: { status, redirectTo }`; load only while `canLoad` is true. Only a confirmed `unauthenticated` status redirects (with `state.returnTo`); `loading` and `unavailable` wait. Example: `useListRoute(() => ({ selections: { all: { path: '/orders' }, mine: { path: '/orders', query: { view: 'mine' }, requiresAuth: true } }, auth: { status: status.value, redirectTo: '/login' } }))`, with `const { status } = useAuth()` from `@molecule/app-vue`.

A one-time credential (reset token or OAuth `code`): `const token = useConsumedSearchParam('token')` from `@molecule/app-vue` keeps the value and removes that URL key; read `token.value[0]`, clear it with `token.value[1]('')`. `src/main.ts` wires `createVueRouter({ router })` with `setRouter` and passes it to `moleculePlugin`; keep that wiring.

@molecule/app-state.label: State Management

@molecule/app-react: React binding: a toggle or counter button uses `useOptimisticValue({ value, commit, equals })` from `@molecule/app-react`, with `value` from the record's props or query and `commit` sending one change and returning the server's value. Render `value`, call `update((current) => next)` on every click, and give the component a `key` per record.

React toggle: const enabled = useOptimisticValue({ value: record.enabled, commit: async (desiredEnabled) => saveEnabled(record.id, desiredEnabled) }); render enabled.value and call enabled.update((current) => !current) on click. commit receives the DESIRED state; a false current flag must send true to enable. The save must return the confirmed boolean, or map its response to that boolean. Give the mounted control a key per record and keep it mounted during refetches. Local UI toggles can use useState.

For a boolean with any application-owned markup, use `useOptimisticToggle({ value, commit })` from `@molecule/app-react`: render its value and use onClick={toggle}. toggle() takes no argument; commit(desired) saves the DESIRED boolean and must return the server-confirmed boolean. Keep the loaded, keyed control mounted and enabled while saving. Local UI switches without a server commit stay plain local state.
@molecule/app-ui-react: For a server-backed boolean button, render `OptimisticToggleButton` from `@molecule/app-ui-react` after its record loads: `<OptimisticToggleButton key={record.id} value={record.enabled} commit={async (desired) => (await saveEnabled(record.id, desired)).enabled} activeLabel={t("disable", undefined, { defaultValue: "Disable" })} inactiveLabel={t("enable", undefined, { defaultValue: "Enable" })} />`. It renders both action labels, changes the label immediately, saves in order, and rolls back a failed save. Keep authorization and self-record checks in the app, and keep the keyed button mounted during refetches. Local UI switches stay local.
@molecule/app-vue: Vue binding: a toggle or counter button uses `useOptimisticValue(() => ({ value, commit, equals }))` from `@molecule/app-vue`, with `value` from the record's props or query and `commit` sending one change and returning the server's value. The getter hands each new server value to the same component. Render `value`, call `update((current) => next)` on every click, and mount one component per record (`:key="record.id"`).

Vue toggle: const { value: enabled, update } = useOptimisticValue(() => ({ value: props.record.enabled, commit: async (desiredEnabled) => saveEnabled(props.record.id, desiredEnabled) })); render enabled in the template and call update((current) => !current) on click. commit receives the DESIRED state; a false current flag must send true to enable. The save must return the confirmed boolean, or map its response to that boolean. Mount one control per record and keep it mounted during refetches. Local UI toggles can use ref.
@molecule/app-ui-vue: For a server-backed boolean button, render `OptimisticToggleButton` from `@molecule/app-ui-vue` after its record loads: `<OptimisticToggleButton :key="record.id" :value="record.enabled" :commit="async (desired) => (await saveEnabled(record.id, desired)).enabled" :active-label="t('disable', undefined, { defaultValue: 'Disable' })" :inactive-label="t('enable', undefined, { defaultValue: 'Enable' })" />`. It renders both action labels, changes the label immediately, saves in order, and rolls back a failed save. Keep authorization and self-record checks in the app, and keep the button mounted during refetches. Local UI switches stay local.
@molecule/app-solid: Solid binding: a toggle or counter button uses `useOptimisticValue(() => ({ value, commit, equals }))` from `@molecule/app-solid`, with `value` from the record's props or query and `commit` sending one change and returning the server's value. The accessor hands each new server value to the same component. Render `value`, call `update((current) => next)` on every click, and mount one component per record (`<For each={records()}>`, or `<Show when={record()} keyed>` for one record).

Solid toggle: const enabled = useOptimisticValue(() => ({ value: props.record.enabled, commit: async (desiredEnabled) => saveEnabled(props.record.id, desiredEnabled) })); render enabled.value() and call enabled.update((current) => !current) on click. commit receives the DESIRED state; a false current flag must send true to enable. The save must return the confirmed boolean, or map its response to that boolean. Mount one control per record and keep it mounted during refetches. Local UI toggles can use createSignal.
@molecule/app-ui-solid: For a server-backed boolean button, render `OptimisticToggleButton` from `@molecule/app-ui-solid` after its record loads: `<OptimisticToggleButton value={record.enabled} commit={async (desired) => (await saveEnabled(record.id, desired)).enabled} activeLabel={t("disable", undefined, { defaultValue: "Disable" })} inactiveLabel={t("enable", undefined, { defaultValue: "Enable" })} />` once per record, inside `<For each={records()}>` or `<Show when={record()} keyed>`. It renders both action labels, changes the label immediately, saves in order, and rolls back a failed save. Keep authorization and self-record checks in the app, and keep the button mounted during refetches. Local UI switches stay local.
@molecule/app-svelte: Svelte binding: a toggle or counter button uses `useOptimisticValue(toStore(() => ({ value, commit, equals })))` from `@molecule/app-svelte`, with `value` from the record's props or query and `commit` sending one change and returning the server's value. The store (`toStore` from "svelte/store") hands each new server value to the same component. Render `value`, call `update((current) => next)` on every click, and mount one component per record (`{#each records as record (record.id)}` or `{#key record.id}`).

Svelte toggle: const { value: enabled, update } = useOptimisticValue(toStore(() => ({ value: record.enabled, commit: async (desiredEnabled) => saveEnabled(record.id, desiredEnabled) }))); render $enabled and call update((current) => !current) on click. commit receives the DESIRED state; a false current flag must send true to enable. The save must return the confirmed boolean, or map its response to that boolean. Mount one control per record and keep it mounted during refetches. Local UI toggles can use $state.
@molecule/app-ui-svelte: For a server-backed boolean button, render `OptimisticToggleButton` from `@molecule/app-ui-svelte` after its record loads: `{#key record.id}<OptimisticToggleButton value={record.enabled} commit={async (desired) => (await saveEnabled(record.id, desired)).enabled} activeLabel={t("disable", undefined, { defaultValue: "Disable" })} inactiveLabel={t("enable", undefined, { defaultValue: "Enable" })} />{/key}`. It renders both action labels, changes the label immediately, saves in order, and rolls back a failed save. Keep authorization and self-record checks in the app, and keep the button mounted during refetches. Local UI switches stay local.
@molecule/app-angular: Angular binding: a toggle or counter button uses `useOptimisticValue(computed(() => ({ value, commit, equals })))` from `@molecule/app-angular`, with `value` from the record's props or query and `commit` sending one change and returning the server's value. Call it in a component field; the computed hands each new server value to the same component. Render `value`, call `update((current) => next)` on every click, and mount one component per record (`@for (record of records(); track record.id)`).

Angular toggle: readonly enabled = useOptimisticValue(computed(() => ({ value: this.record().enabled, commit: async (desiredEnabled: boolean) => saveEnabled(this.record().id, desiredEnabled) }))); render enabled.value() and call enabled.update((current) => !current) on click. commit receives the DESIRED state; a false current flag must send true to enable. The save must return the confirmed boolean, or map its response to that boolean. Mount one control per record and keep it mounted during refetches. Local UI toggles can use signal.
@molecule/app-ui-angular: For a server-backed boolean button, render `OptimisticToggleButton` from `@molecule/app-ui-angular` after its record loads: `<button mol-optimistic-toggle-button [value]="record().enabled" [commit]="commit" [activeLabel]="disableLabel" [inactiveLabel]="enableLabel"></button>` in a component per record (`record = input.required<MyRecord>()`, rendered inside `@for (record of records(); track record.id)`), with `commit = async (desired: boolean) => (await saveEnabled(this.record().id, desired)).enabled` and the two labels from t(). It renders both action labels, changes the label immediately, saves in order, and rolls back a failed save. Keep authorization and self-record checks in the app, and keep the button mounted during refetches. Local UI switches stay local.

configuration: A server-backed value the person toggles or sets (favorite, follow, like, bookmark, rating, quantity, a setting switch): use `createOptimisticValue({ value, commit, equals })`. It shows each change at once and saves one change at a time; a tap during a save is saved right after it, and only a failure of the newest change goes back to the server value. Never ignore a tap or disable the control while a save is pending, and never let a refetch or new props replace the value during a save.

@molecule/app-stepper-default.quickStart:
import { setProvider, requireProvider } from '@molecule/app-stepper'
import { provider } from '@molecule/app-stepper-default'

setProvider(provider)

const steps = [
  { id: 'account', label: 'Account', completed: false },
  { id: 'profile', label: 'Profile', completed: false },
  { id: 'review', label: 'Review', completed: false, optional: true },
]
const stepper = requireProvider().createStepper({
  steps,
  linear: true,
  onStepChange: (i) => render(i),
})

// Linear mode reads YOUR step objects: mark the current one complete to unlock next().
steps[stepper.getActiveStep()].completed = true
stepper.next()

configuration: Server-backed boolean buttons: use OptimisticToggleButton with a loaded value, commit(desired) returning the saved boolean, and complete activeLabel and inactiveLabel actions (for example Unwatch equipment and Watch equipment). Both labels are required; label and aria-pressed follow the displayed state.

Mount after the initial record loads, key by record identity, and keep the control mounted during refetches. Use createQueryResource().toggle() for a POST/DELETE relationship. Use useOptimisticValue with local markup for a flag plus related count; keep ordinary Button or Switch for local-only state.

intentHints: protected route for an authenticated session
auth route guard to protect routes
watch unwatch button with a stateful action label
@molecule/app-ui-react.quickStart:
import { setClassMap } from '@molecule/app-ui'
import { classMap } from '@molecule/app-ui-tailwind'
import { Button, Modal, Icon, EmptyState } from '@molecule/app-ui-react'
import { useState } from 'react'

// Once at startup, before first render — components throw without it:
setClassMap(classMap)

function ConfirmDelete({ onConfirm }: { onConfirm: () => void }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  return (
    <>
      <Button color="error" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        <Icon name="trash" size={16} /> Delete
      </Button>
      <Modal
        open={open}
        onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
        title="Delete item?"
        data-mol-id="confirm-delete"
      >
        <EmptyState title="This cannot be undone" />
        <Button color="error" onClick={onConfirm}>
          Confirm
        </Button>
      </Modal>
    </>
  )
}

@parcel/watcher.reason: Compiles the watcher only when npm_config_build_from_source is true; the prebuilt binary comes in its optional @parcel/watcher-<platform> package.

bcrypt.reason: node-gyp-build loads the prebuilt binary the tarball ships for linux, darwin and win32 (glibc and musl) and compiles only when none matches.

better-sqlite3.reason: Loads the prebuilt binary the tarball ships in prebuilds/ for linux (glibc and musl), darwin and win32 on x64 and arm64; node-gyp builds one only on other platforms.

esbuild.reason: Checks and links the platform binary from its optional @esbuild/<platform> package; esbuild finds that binary at run time without it.

fsevents.reason: Rebuilds fsevents.node with node-gyp; the tarball already ships the built fsevents.node.

lmdb.reason: Loads the prebuilt binary from its optional @lmdb/lmdb-<platform> package and compiles only when none matches.

msgpackr-extract.reason: Loads the prebuilt binary from its optional @msgpackr-extract/<platform> package; msgpackr falls back to JavaScript without it.

onnxruntime-node.reason: Downloads the CUDA execution provider on linux/x64; the CPU binaries ship in the tarball.

protobufjs.reason: Warns when a dependent's version range uses another scheme.

puppeteer.reason: Downloads the Chrome build puppeteer drives; without it launch() fails unless an executablePath is given.
